title: In-Context Learning for Pure Exploration
claim: An agent alternates between actively querying its environment and then inferring the hypothesis from the collected data, shown on a concrete example.
layout: 2 panels: left image-patch sequence, right cyclic loop then arrow to inference
description: The figure has two panels. Panel (a), on the left, is a row of seven small black-and-gray image frames showing a generalized search example. Each frame starts nearly masked and gradually reveals more patches. The newly revealed patch in each frame is outlined in red. The last frame is overlaid with a blue grid and red markers, which shows the final inferred label. Panel (b), on the right, is a schematic with two phases. In the Exploration Phase, a circular loop connects a policy node π_t(·|D_t) at the top to a globe icon representing the environment. The action a_t goes down on the right and the observation x_{t+1} comes back on the left. A wide gray arrow labeled D_N leads to the Inference Phase, which shows Ĥ_N = I_N(·|D_N). Everything is on a white background with serif math text.
caption: { (a)} Generalized search example: \icpe{} starts from a masked image (left), and sequentially reveals patches expected to reduce the posterior entropy over labels. It stops once the inferred label is $\delta$-correct (right). { (b)} After executing an action $a_t$, the agent observes $x_{t+1}$. At inference time, the data collected is used to infer an hypothesis.
abstract: We study the problem active sequential hypothesis testing, also known as pure exploration: given a new task, the learner adaptively collects data from the environment to efficiently determine an underlying correct hypothesis. A classical instance of this problem is the task of identifying the best arm in a multi-armed bandit problem (a.k.a. BAI, Best-Arm Identification), where actions index hypotheses. Another important case is generalized search, a problem of determining the correct label through a sequence of strategically selected queries that indirectly reveal information about the label. In this work, we introduce In-Context Pure Explorer (ICPE), which meta-trains Transformers to map observation histories to query actions and a predicted hypothesis, yielding a model that transfers in-context. At inference time, ICPE actively gathers evidence on new tasks and infers the true hypothesis without parameter updates. Across deterministic, stochastic, and structured benchmarks, including BAI and generalized search, ICPE is competitive with adaptive baselines while requiring no explicit modeling of information structure. Our results support Transformers as practical architectures for general sequential testing.
